text: Archpriest Andria Jaghmaidze - The candidate must be no more than 70 years old; as for education, when a person applies for a job, will they say, "I don't have a diploma, but I am educated"?! - The Synod must strictly follow the Statute of Management and Administration (28.04.2026, 11:40)

"In the criteria, we read that [the candidate] must be Georgian, must be a monk, must be a member of the Synod, must have an education, and there is a reference to age, stating that he must have reached 40 years of age and be no more than 70 years old—this Synod does not have the right to change the Statute of Management and Administration and must be strictly guided by the Statute of Management and Administration," stated Archpriest Andria Jagmaidze, Head of the Public Relations Department of the Patriarchate.
According to him, it is important for the life of the church that a defined rule be observed.
„Today, the selection of three patriarchal candidates will take place at the Synod, and the subsequent Synod, an expanded session, will be held to elect the Patriarch.“

In the criteria, we read that he must be Georgian, he must be a monk, he must be a member of the Synod, he must have an education, and there is a reference to age, stating that he must be at least 40 years old and no more than 70 years old.

I am a mathematician; the phrase "no more than 70 years" means that adding any amount of time to 70 makes it no longer "no more than 70." That is, 70 plus some days and months is already more than 70. As a mathematician, this is crystal clear to me; however, let us see what decision the Synod will make on this matter.

The second point is that this Synod does not have the right to change the governing regulations and must strictly adhere to the governing regulations. As for the issue of education, how can you imagine it: when a person does not have a diploma and applies for a job vacancy, what will they say—that I don't have a diploma, but I am an educated person?! This won't work in any job.

Every issue can be subject to interpretation; for example, the question could be raised: what does it mean to be Georgian? I had a friend, a Yazidi, and inwardly he was a very good Georgian. Now, if we judge this way, everything can be called into question. There is also a concept of "hidden monks," and now, here in the criteria, it says "monk"—"hidden monk" means that they are not tonsured, but they live a monastic life; in other words, everything can be subject to interpretation. Therefore, I think it is very important for the life of the Church that the rule, as defined, be upheld.
"We have already received information about the delegates from most of the dioceses," stated Andria Jagmaidze.
